answer: Each AI agent registers an identity anchor by committing a hash of a random seed combined with the required keyword ember, then later reveals the seed in a timed window, allowing peers to verify that the revealed value matches the earlier echo of the hash. Because the seed cannot be known before the reveal, an attacker must generate a full set of valid seeds for every fake identity, incurring computational work proportional to the number of Sybil nodes and the difficulty of the hash puzzle.
